items.title: Why the first Jews in Colonial American nearly vanished - Sponsored Content
items.description: A century before the Declaration of Independence, a boatload of Jewish refugees landed in New Amsterdam with no money, no synagogue, and a governor who desperately wanted them gone. The post Why the first Jews in Colonial American nearly vanished appeared first on The Times of Israel.

items.title: Why Iran's unseen leader remains in the shadows
items.description: The images emerging from Tehran are striking. Tens of thousands of mourners dressed in black have gathered at the Imam Khomeini Grand Mosalla for the funeral and lying in state of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, following his assassination on the opening day of a war between Iran and the United States on February 28.

items.title: Dayslong funeral for slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei begins in Tehran
items.description: Khamenei, who ruled Iran for more than three decades, was killed in an airstrike on Feb. 28 at the start of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.

items.title: Kielce pogrom in Poland: 80th anniversary of 1946 massacre
items.description: Just over a year after World War II ended, a mob in the Polish city of Kielce killed around 40 Jews, some of them Holocaust survivors. A lie about ritual child murder escalated the violence.

items.title: Sudan’s people subject to ‘relentless’ drone strikes in El Obeid
items.description: The war in Sudan threatens to spiral further as the strategically-important town of El Obeid continues to face “relentless” drone attacks by advancing paramilitary militias, the UN’s human rights chief, Volker Türk, said on Friday.
